messages:
Maya (AcmeAI): Hey team — we just started a large embeddings job against embedding-large-v2 and are getting a ton of 429s. Job is ~1.2M docs, batch_size=256, 8 workers parallel. Errors started after ~10 minutes and now ~30% of requests are 429ing. Sample error: "429 Too Many Requests" and headers showing Retry-After: 6. Some embeddings that do return have wrong dimensions (expected 1536, got 1024) which is breaking our downstream pipeline. We're blocked — can someone advise immediate mitigations and root cause? Account: acme-ai-prod.

Anna (Support): Sorry you're hitting this — we can help. First quick mitigations you can try immediately:
- reduce concurrency and flatten burst (lower number of parallel workers from 8 -> 2)
- reduce batch_size from 256 -> 64
- implement exponential backoff with jitter honoring Retry-After
- check response headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After

Can you paste a sample raw response headers (if available) and confirm the exact model name you're sending in the request payload? Also opening a temporary support ticket and asking Eng to look at burst token exhaustion.

Jordan (Eng Runtime): Adding context from runtime: our embeddings path enforces two quotas for accounts — a long-term per-second token (requests/sec) quota and a burst token bucket with refill rate. Large parallel batches can exhaust the burst bucket quickly; when the bucket is empty we return 429s with Retry-After to signal cooldown. Also, if a request is routed to a fallback/compatible model variant (we do this to keep throughput available under tight capacity), that can return a smaller-dimension embedding leading to the dimension mismatch you saw.

Immediate actions:
- Pin the model version in your call (model: "embedding-large-v2@v2.1" or exact model id) — this prevents automatic fallback to a smaller variant.
- Throttle concurrency per process (concurrency 1-2) and let the platform do autoscaling rather than many parallel clients.
- Limit batch_size to 32-64 for steady throughput; very large batches can spike token consumption and trigger burst limits.

Sample curl to show header check:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"embedding-large-v2@v2.1","input":["text1","text2"]}'
```
Look for headers: Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Limit

Kevin (SRE): We can provision a short, temporary quota bump (burst smoothing) while you drain the job, but please reduce concurrency first or the bump will be consumed fast. I've opened internal ticket INC-20260315-47 for the bump request and Eng follow-up. For production, we recommend smoothing client concurrency and implementing backoff.

Anna (Support): Also send us 1) request id from a failing response (x-request-id) and 2) a small repro script/steps. We'll attach to the internal ticket. Meanwhile try this backoff snippet (python) — full jitter is important when many workers retry:
```
import random, time
base = 0.5
cap = 15.0
for attempt in range(1, 6):
    sleep = min(cap, base * 2 ** (attempt - 1))
    jitter = random.random() * sleep
    time.sleep(jitter)
    # retry request
```

Maya (AcmeAI): We have x-request-id: req_0a6f1e and a sample failing response headers: Retry-After: 6, X-RateLimit-Limit: 120/min, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0. We're going to scale down workers now. The dimension mismatch is odd — we always send model param. Could the fallback happen silently?

Jordan (Eng Runtime): If you send a vague model name (e.g., "embedding-large-v2" without version) the router may select a compatible variant in constrained situations. Always include explicit model version (or model id) to avoid fallback. Also check your client retries: if your retry path omits the model param for some code paths, that could cause a routed fallback. We'll instrument the request id you gave to see if it was served by a fallback model. Quick heuristics:
- Check embedding length: 1536 expected. If 1024 returned, it was likely a smaller variant.
- Check our response header "X-Model-Served" (we include model id in responses when available).

Kevin (SRE): For your long-run job, consider chunking the job into smaller workers with queueing and rate-limiting (token bucket at the client). This avoids synchronized bursts. If you use async workers, add a central concurrency limiter.

Maya (AcmeAI): After dropping to 2 workers and batch_size=64 plus adding the jitter backoff, we saw 429s drop to <1% over the next 10m. One returned embedding still had 1024 dims though — I'll paste that response.

Anna (Support): Thanks — leaving the internal ticket open. We'll request logs from runtime for req_0a6f1e and follow up with whether that specific request hit a fallback model. If we find a server-side routing bug we'll roll a fix. If you want a temporary quota bump while you re-ingest the backlog manually, reply with the desired extra RPS and approximate window; we'll route through sales/ops for approval.

rate-limiter-bot: Policy notice — account acme-ai-prod hit embeddings burst threshold at 2026-03-15T14:02:10Z. Actions: 429 responses issued until cooldown; recommend reducing concurrent clients. More info: https://console.redwood.ai/account/usage

Jordan (Eng Runtime): Follow-up items for us: check routing logs for the request id and confirm whether fallback served smaller model, and audit router logic around explicit vs ambiguous model names. For you: pin model version, throttle concurrency, use batch sizes <= 64, implement exponential backoff with full jitter, and monitor X-RateLimit headers to shape client behavior.

Maya (AcmeAI): Great — applying changes now. We'll also export the failing request/response and paste here if it pops again. Thanks everyone for quick help.
